# Deepest-energy optimality, critical quantiles, and retained base work

This note gives the exact finite-dimensional optimality statement for an
energy-maximal actual deepest point. It distinguishes an unconditional
closed-cone statement from a finite EXACT critical-cap multiplier formula,
which can require a constraint qualification. It also gives an actual
nonaffine calibration showing why the resulting continuous-normal identity
does not identify a global positive chart with a positive sum of critical
ambient margins.

The family is a finite complete positive compatible family `K_z`, `d>=1`,
with its canonical fiber hull and mixed measure `mu`. Let `Q>0` be its
actual global raw maximum depth and `D={Y:D_mu(Y)>=Q}` its real depth
superlevel set. At a selected base `p`, write

    D_p={x:(p,x) in D}.

Choose `y in D_p` maximizing `E_(K_p)(y)` over `D_p`; in particular this
holds at a point of the maximal stratum in
`candidate ce31fbbf06cede9c`.
All these points are interior to their own fibers. The set `D_p` is compact
and convex, but can have empty interior or be a singleton. Let `a` be the
unique projective minimizer at `y`.

## 1. The unconditional constrained optimum

Use the outward convex normal-cone convention

    N_(D_p)(y)={v:v.(x-y)<=0 for every x in D_p}.

The envelope derivative and concavity give the exact equivalence

    y maximizes E_(K_p) on D_p  iff  a in N_(D_p)(y),    (1)

since `grad E=(d+1)E a` and the factor is positive. Necessity follows by
differentiating every feasible segment from `y`; sufficiency follows from
the concave tangent inequality for `E^(1/d)`. No constraint qualification,
depth differentiability, or smoothness of the fiber boundary is used.

If `y` is interior to `D_p`, (1) forces `a=0`, so `y` is the ordinary
own-fiber centroid. If `D_p={y}`, (1) imposes NO restriction on `a`.
An attained minimum over shapes is not needed for (1), and it supplies
no body-variation stationarity by itself.

## 2. Actual quantile halfspaces, including all closed boundaries

Normalize the continuous normal to `|u|=1` and allow an arbitrary base
tilt `b in R^n`. Define

    T_(b,u)(t)=mu{(z,x):b.z+u.x>=t},
    tau_(b,u)=sup{t:T_(b,u)(t)>=Q}.

These tails are continuous because every fiber has positive continuous
dimension and `u!=0`. They run from total mass to zero, so the finite
upper quantile satisfies `T_(b,u)(tau)=Q`. Put

    c_(b,u)=tau_(b,u)-b.p-u.y>=0.                        (2)

Then the exact feasible-source set is

    D_p-y=intersection_(b,u){h:u.h<=c_(b,u)}.            (3)

Pure integer halfspaces impose conditions independent of the continuous
source point; they are already satisfied at the chosen deepest base and
therefore add no constraint to (3). This does not discard their closed
boundary mass from depth. Points outside `K_p` have zero depth by a
strict support separation and the finite affine support majorant, so
(3) does not accidentally add extraneous candidate points.

An index is active precisely when `c_(b,u)=0`. Its actual cap through
`(p,y)` has mass `Q` and a positive proper own section. Conversely every
nonvertical critical containing cap can be moved to the source boundary;
a strict margin would remove positive own volume and contradict depth
`Q`. Thus the active indices are exactly the nonvertical critical caps.

## 3. Exact lifted-cone alternative; no implicit minimax swap

Let `G` be the set of vectors `(u,c_(b,u))` in `R^(d+1)`. Then

    a in N_(D_p)(y)
      iff (a,0) in closure(cone G).                    (4)

One direction follows by applying each conic combination to a feasible
`h` in (3), then taking the limit; its total slack tends to zero.
For the converse, if `(a,0)` is outside the closed cone, finite-dimensional
separation gives `(h,s)` with

    a.h>0,  u.h+s c_(b,u)<=0 for every index.

If `s>=0`, then `u.h<=0<=c` and `h` is feasible in (3), a contradiction.
If `s<0`, the vector `h/(-s)` is feasible and still has positive pairing
with `a`, again a contradiction. This proves (4) directly.

By conic Caratheodory in dimension `d+1`, (4) is equivalent to the following
finite approximate certificates. For every `epsilon>0`, there are at most
`d+1` actual quantile caps and coefficients `lambda_j>=0` such that

    |a-sum_j lambda_j u_j|<=epsilon,
    0<=sum_j lambda_j c_j<=epsilon.                     (5)

The caps in (5) need not be exactly critical and the multipliers need
not stay bounded. Both qualifications are essential to this unconditional
statement. It is not permissible to discard the slacks and declare an
exact active-cap KKT formula without an additional argument.

## 4. When genuine finite critical-cap multipliers follow

A precise sufficient condition is bounded multipliers in certificates
(5). In that case a convergent subsequence gives

    a=sum_(j=1)^m lambda_j u_j,
    lambda_j>=0,  c_j=0,  m<=d,                         (6)

with actual critical caps. Here is the compactness detail for the active
normals, so it is not an assumed compactification of arbitrary tilts.
For a quantile cap with small `c`, write its fiber threshold as
`u.y+c-b.(z-p)`. Proper fiber thresholds determine bounded values of
`b.(z-p)`; full and zero-volume traces impose one-sided linear inequalities
with bounded right-hand sides. A replacement tilt can be chosen as the
minimum-norm solution of this feasible fixed-matrix system. The finite
independent-active-row formulas bound it uniformly. It preserves every
fiber's cap VOLUME, including full/zero supporting statuses up to null
`d`-volume. Since the own trace is proper when `c` is small, the same
threshold is still the upper `Q` quantile. Compactness and continuity
of the actual nonvertical cap volume then turn every limiting positive-
multiplier term into a genuine critical cap. Terms whose multiplier
tends to zero disappear. Ordinary conic Caratheodory reduces the resulting
representation from at most `d+1` to at most `d` normals in `R^d`.

For example, boundedness follows from a Slater ball `w+rB subset D_p`,
`r>0`. Every normalized inequality has
`c-u.(w-y)>=r`; summing a certificate gives

    r sum lambda_j <= sum lambda_j c_j
                         -(sum lambda_j u_j).(w-y),

whose right-hand side is bounded as (5) improves. Another sufficient
condition is that finitely many actual quantile inequalities define
`D_p` locally at `y`; the usual finite polyhedral normal-cone formula
then applies, even without full-dimensional Slater interior.

The need for care is already visible in an ordinary infinite linear
system. In coordinates `(s,t)`, impose

    t>=2r s-r^2 for every r in [-1,1],  t<=0.

Its feasible set is the singleton `(0,0)`. At that point the only active
displayed normals are vertical, while its normal cone is all of `R^2`.
This is a constraint-qualification warning, NOT an assertion that this
particular system has been realized as a mixed depth region.

Conversely, if some genuine critical continuous normals positively span
`R^d`, their through-source inequalities already force `D_p={y}` and
their cone is all of `R^d`. Then (6) is automatic for EVERY vector `a`.
In that common full-circuit regime, the finite KKT formula by itself is
vacuous as a quantitative payment restriction.

## 5. Exact section factors and nonsmooth supporting traces

For a fixed active cap, retain its displayed continuous normal `u` and
its actual coarea factor `1/|u|`. Let `S_P` be the sum of proper-section
coareas, `S_F` the sum of full-side supporting-facet coareas, and `S_E`
the sum of empty-side supporting-facet coareas. Strictly saturated traces
contribute zero. The own section is proper, so `S_P>0`.

When its boundary is moved through `(p,y+h)` without changing its normal
or base tilt, put `s=u.h`. The exact first directional cap-mass change is

    -S_P s-S_F(s)_+ +S_E(-s)_+.                         (7)

This follows from the one-sided limiting section densities. Full-side
support loses mass only when the threshold increases; empty-side support
gains mass only when it decreases. Formula (7) is valid also in `d=1`,
with section counting measure and the same closed-cap conventions.

For a support-free regular cap its constraint derivative is `S_P u`.
Thus (6), when valid, can be written as

    (d+1)E a=sum_j eta_j S_(P,j) u_j,  eta_j>=0.         (8)

At supporting caps the two actual one-sided positive scales are
`S_P+S_F` and `S_P+S_E`. Either can rescale a conormal multiplier, but
(7), not a freely chosen allocation, is the actual directional derivative.
The geometric normal to the quantile feasible halfspace remains `u` in
all cases because both one-sided scales are strictly positive.

The coefficients in (6) or (8) are objective normal-cone multipliers.
They are NOT automatically the response weights of a chosen critical
cover, nor the inside/outside supporting allocations in the generic
normal-stress theorem. Identifying those different variables would be
an additional unproved condition.

## 6. What the multiplier relation really says about a global chart

Suppose (6) holds, and write each actual critical margin as

    m_j(z,x)=u_j.(x-y)+b_j.(z-p),  H_j={m_j>=0}.

For ANY globally positive affine chart with the prescribed source
parameter, `L=1+a.(x-y)+b.(z-p)`, the exact identity is only

    L=1+sum_j lambda_j m_j
           +[b-sum_j lambda_j b_j].(z-p).               (9)

The remaining base work has no sign prescribed by (1) or (6). For an
approximate certificate (5), add the exact terms `sum lambda_j c_j`
and `(a-sum lambda_j u_j).(x-y)` to (9), using the actual shifted
quantile margins. The base work remains; it need not be small.

The projective cut fields contain a nonlinear inverse power of `L`, so
even (9) with zero base work would not turn their cap losses into a linear
combination of normal multipliers. No new signed payment follows merely
from this rewrite. The following actual example makes the nonzero base
work issue explicit.

## 7. Actual nonaffine energy-selected calibration

Use the independently certified global-depth family in
`candidate c0a17a15efbe8efa`
and its projective normalizer in
`candidate e0241fcf7902a02f`:

    h=20/97, t=100/291, e=1/100,
    K_r={(x1,x2):x1,x2>=0, h<=x1+x2<=r},
    C_z=K_(1+e z),  -1<=z<=1,
    Y=(0,t,t).

There are exactly three integer fibers. The certified critical caps are

    H1: x1+x2<=2t,
    H2: t x1+(3t-1)x2-e t z>=t(4t-1),
    H3: (3t-1)x1+t x2-e t z>=t(4t-1).                   (10)

They have common global raw mass `Q=18200/28227`; each endpoint's entire
area is strictly smaller than `Q`. Any other deepest point in the middle
fiber must have nonpositive margin in all three caps: a positive margin
would permit a threshold increase retaining it while deleting positive
proper-section volume. The positive circuit then forces all margins to
be zero, whose intersection is the single point `(t,t)`. Thus `Y` is the
unique actual deepest point, so it is automatically energy-selected.

Its nonzero minimizing projective parameter is `a=(c,c)`, where

    c=(44426-1067 sqrt(1702))/25480>0.

The cited source proves this root is admissible and uniquely stationary.
Using the unnormalized normals in (10), every nonnegative representation
of `a` has coefficients

    lambda_2=lambda_3=s,
    lambda_1=(4t-1)s-c,
    s>=c/(4t-1)>0.

Consequently EVERY such representation of this selected critical menu
has strictly negative combined base component

    sum_j lambda_j b_j=-2e t s<0.                       (11)

On the other hand, the energy-supergradient positive chart has a strictly
positive base component. Let `E=E_(K_1)(t,t)` and
`L_top=1+c(1-2t)`. The explicit section integral for the varying upper
facet and the envelope identity give

    partial_z E_(K_(1+e z))(t,t)|_(z=0)=e L_top^(-3)>0.

Thus its normalized root-energy base derivative is
`B=e L_top^(-3)/(2E)`, and the global chart of the energy-supergradient
lemma has

    b_E=(2/3)B=e L_top^(-3)/(3E)>0.                     (12)

Equations (11)--(12) show that the actual energy chart's ambient affine
normal cannot be the nonnegative sum of this critical menu's ambient
normals, although its continuous normal is exactly such a sum. The base
correction in (9) is necessarily `b_E+2e t s>0`.

This correction does not disappear by a whole-measure barycenter identity:
the original mixed base moment is

    integral z dmu=|K_(1+e)|-|K_(1-e)|=2e>0.

The actual critical SECTION base moments, in contrast, are zero, as
required by their regular criticality. They do not license discarding
base work in whole-body or boundary-field integrals.

This is a safe above-target family, not a hypothetical bad attained
minimum or an OC counterexample. It proves an exact obstruction to the
claimed automatic chart/cap-normal identification. A bad-depth or
shape-minimum hypothesis would have to supply an additional relation;
the present KKT condition does not provide it.

## 8. Relation to the generic stress route

Equations (1)--(8) are a finite-dimensional normal-cone specialization
for the distinguished energy objective. They add a precise objective
gradient and retain the depth plateau, quantile slack and supporting
section qualifications. They do not replace the generic normal-stress
conditions on compatible body variations.

The precise archived comparisons are
`candidate a68c14b477a24d06` and
`candidate 9c6d3cb586898f7e`.
The latter concerns cap-normal optimality and keeps EVERY inside
supporting-facet allocation with a corresponding outside allocation.
Those quantifiers are independent of maximizing energy over the source
depth region and are not reduced to the scalar threshold branches in
Section 5 here.

For a full-rank critical circuit at a singleton deepest point they give
no restriction beyond conic representability of an arbitrary vector.
For a nontrivial plateau they can constrain its energy maximizer, but no
inequality controlling the residual base work or the nonlinear signed
global-cut costs has been proved here. This bounded interface is therefore
not a closure of the arbitrary-rank variational route.
